scope: Research baseline for JNAP root design, reusable personal PR templates, and future client design pitches.

sources.title: Paco Coursey
sources.research_role: Shows how a personal root can make projects, writing, now, and contact feel direct without a marketing wrapper.
usable_lessons: Let visible work and routes carry credibility.
Use simple labels and strong information scent.
Keep the page personal without turning it into a bio essay.
avoid: Copying developer-only category language.
Letting minimalism become generic.

sources.title: Brian Lovin
sources.research_role: Shows a mature personal site where writing, projects, tools, listening, and professional identity coexist.
usable_lessons: A personal site can be a living index instead of a static resume.
Project lists can create trust when they are specific and easy to scan.
Personal and professional signals can share the same surface.
avoid: Making the root feel like a blog index only.
Over-indexing on software-insider references for general visitors.

sources.title: Agencies | Joe Coleman
sources.research_role: Shows how direct listing can communicate credibility without explanatory copy.
usable_lessons: Proof can be terse when the structure is confident.
Dense credibility can work when navigation remains obvious.
A list can be more memorable than a polished claim.
avoid: Desktop-only density.
Making proof feel like an opaque insider roll call.

sources.title: Anime.js | JavaScript Animation Engine
sources.research_role: Shows how motion and interactive examples can create curiosity while still supporting documentation and navigation.
usable_lessons: Motion should reward interaction instead of blocking comprehension.
Interactive craft can be part of the brand signal.
Responsive and modular motion belongs behind clear static structure.
avoid: Animation as spectacle.
Motion required to understand or access routes.
A library-site level of technical density on a personal root.

sources.title: Rauno Freiberg
sources.research_role: Shows how sparse language, rhythm, and restraint can create a memorable personal signature.
usable_lessons: A site can feel authored with very little copy.
Short phrases can become a stronger brand signal than a pitch.
Restraint can make interaction details feel more intentional.
avoid: Copying aphorism structure.
Letting style outrun route clarity.

sources.title: Derek Sivers
sources.research_role: Shows how a personal site can expose biography, now, contact, books, projects, and writing through plain information architecture.
usable_lessons: Plain route labels can build trust quickly.
A personal archive can be broad without hiding the next step.
Direct contact framing can feel human when the rest of the page is organized.
avoid: Becoming text-heavy on the root.
Letting breadth bury the high-signal exits.

sources.title: A Brief History & Ethos of the Digital Garden
sources.research_role: Frames the docs/wiki direction as exploratory, evolving, contextual personal knowledge instead of a reverse-chronological blog.
usable_lessons: The docs/wiki surface should support topology over timeline.
Garden content can be incomplete but useful if its state is legible.
Personal knowledge systems should encourage exploration without making users lost.
avoid: Using garden language as decoration only.
Publishing private or half-ready material without state markers.

sources.title: About Me | Tania Rascia
sources.research_role: Shows how professional work, writing, personal interests, tools, and contact can live in one normal public web space.
usable_lessons: A personal site can be broad without sounding like a pitch.
Clear public boundaries make personal details feel intentional.
A normal human voice can improve trust.
avoid: Overloading the root with every personal detail.
Using personal texture without privacy review.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.research_role: Defines accessibility constraints that every template and interaction must respect.
usable_lessons: Keyboard access, focus visibility, target size, text alternatives, and meaningful structure are baseline requirements.
Motion and interaction cannot interfere with access.
Accessible implementation improves usability beyond compliance.
avoid: Treating accessibility as a post-build checklist.
Relying on visual grouping without programmatic structure.

sources.title: Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10
sources.research_role: Defines the stable token format used to make colors, typography, and spacing portable across templates and future client systems.
usable_lessons: Design decisions should be represented as named tokens when they need to scale.
Token files should separate reusable values from implementation-specific extensions.
A standard token shape improves portability across tools and codebases.
avoid: Hard-coding build-specific CSS as the only source of design truth.
Inventing token structure when a stable format exists.

sources.title: What Are User Stories?
sources.research_role: Provides the user-centered planning pattern used to turn audience intent into build requirements.
usable_lessons: Stories should state who needs what and why.
Stories should guide build choices without over-prescribing implementation.
A story map keeps design work tied to user intent instead of taste alone.
avoid: Writing stories as internal tasks only.
Letting stories replace acceptance criteria.

sources.title: JNAP template research notes, May 2026
sources.research_role: Captures the direction that the root should be mobile-first, experience-first, brand-forward, direct, beautiful, and less like a tech pitch deck.
usable_lessons: Make people interested enough to click further.
Show and do instead of explaining.
Treat the current root as one template, then compare future templates through contracts.
avoid: Generic SaaS hero patterns.
Visible category language that explains obvious groups.
Over-polished pitch-deck tone.
